exposure: Thoracoamniotic shunting (TAS) with a double-basket catheter for fetal hydrothorax (FHT)
outcome: Requirement for oxygen or other respiratory support
Catheter associated problems (dislocation, obstruction, preterm rupture of the membranes)
cohort: The study participants were 295 fetuses with fetal hydrothorax who underwent thoracoamniotic shunting (TAS) with a double-basket catheter, enrolled between 2011 and 2019.
finding: The study reported a favorable 1-year survival rate of 70.5% for fetuses with isolated fetal hydrothorax treated with the double-basket catheter, identifying TAS before 29.5 weeks of gestation and skin edema/ascites as risk factors for death, and appropriate shunt location for >28 days as a protective factor.
gest_age: TAS performed before 29.5 weeks of gestation was identified as a risk factor for death at one year.
